If you can share the relevant file(s) — the route tree/node struct and the matching function — I can trace through exactly how `:name` segments get captured. Alternatively, if you're asking generically (not about a specific codebase), the common approach is:

- The tree has a distinct node type/branch for parameter segments (vs. static segments).
- During matching, when a path segment doesn't match any static child, the matcher checks for a param child, consumes that segment as the value, and records it (often keyed by the param name stored on the node) into a params map/slice.
- Matching continues recursively/iteratively with the remaining path until exhausted, then params are attached to the request context.
